summary: Jeffrey Yass co-founded Susquehanna International Group, a privately held trading firm whose options and market-making businesses made him one of America's wealthiest financiers. He has become a leading Republican and libertarian donor, with school choice as his most sustained policy priority and SIG's large ByteDance stake placing his financial interests inside the national debate over TikTok.

statements.summary: Jeff and Janine Yass argued that public funding should follow families to the school they choose rather than remain tied to residential assignment.
Yass opposed banning TikTok and argued that restricting a communications platform would harm competition and speech.
Yass said he did not discuss TikTok with Trump during their brief meeting.
Yass described markets and politics through probabilistic outcomes rather than certainty, an approach rooted in poker and options trading.
Yass framed school choice as the political project on which he most wants measurable change during his lifetime.

chapters.title: Probability as formation
chapters.body:
Jeff Yass was born in Queens in 1958 and studied mathematics and economics at Binghamton University. He and future partners treated poker and options trading as related problems of probability, pricing and disciplined risk [[nyt-yass-2022, propublica-yass-2021]].

That background matters because Yass still describes decisions in expected-value terms. It shaped a trading culture willing to make many small, hedged bets rather than one directional wager [[nyt-yass-2022]].

chapters.title: Building Susquehanna
chapters.dek: A private trading firm becomes the source of political capital
chapters.body:
Yass co-founded Susquehanna International Group in 1987. The firm expanded from options into market making, trading and private investment while remaining closely held [[sig-about, nyt-yass-2022]].

Because SIG is private, Yass's wealth and ownership are estimates. Forbes and investigative reporting agree that the firm—and especially its ByteDance investment—accounts for most of his fortune [[forbes-yass-2026, propublica-yass-2021]].

chapters.title: School choice as the central project
chapters.dek: A donor builds policy pressure state by state
chapters.body:
Yass and his wife have supported scholarships and voucher advocacy for decades. In Pennsylvania, their money flows through candidates, policy organizations and charitable vehicles rather than one campaign alone [[ap-school-choice-2023, inside-philanthropy-2026]].

The strategy is national. A $6 million gift to Greg Abbott came during a Texas legislative fight over vouchers, while the couple's own writing argues that public support should follow families to chosen schools [[texas-tribune-yass-2023, yass-inquirer-op-ed-2023]].

chapters.title: Republican money with a libertarian center
chapters.dek: Outside groups provide leverage across factions
chapters.body:
Yass became a principal funder of Club for Growth and libertarian-oriented PACs before joining the very top tier of Republican donors. He often funds outside groups that can intervene in primaries as well as general elections [[fec-yass, nyt-yass-2022]].

OpenSecrets counted Jeff and Janine Yass at roughly $101.1 million in the 2024 federal cycle. Household totals show scale, but this profile's money ledger assigns only contributions matched to Jeff [[opensecrets-2024, fec-yass]].

chapters.title: TikTok, policy and financial interest
chapters.dek: A private holding becomes a national-security controversy
chapters.body:
SIG's early ByteDance investment became enormously valuable. Reporting estimated Yass's personal economic equivalent near seven percent, though no public filing supplies a precise current stake [[wsj-tiktok-2023, axios-tiktok-2024]].

Yass opposed a TikTok ban while donating to lawmakers and groups active in the debate. His brief 2024 meeting with Trump preceded Trump's public reversal, but both said TikTok was not discussed; timing alone does not prove influence [[axios-tiktok-2024, inquirer-yass-2024]].

chapters.title: Taxes and scrutiny
chapters.body:
ProPublica reported that SIG used sophisticated trading structures and fought the IRS over the characterization of income. Yass and the firm maintained that their tax positions complied with law and challenged the investigation's framing [[propublica-yass-2021]].

The dispute is relevant because tax savings increased the capital available for investment and giving, but the public record does not justify treating disputed tax positions as criminal findings [[propublica-yass-2021, nyt-yass-2022]].

chapters.title: Institutions beyond campaigns
chapters.dek: Foundations, think tanks and international policy
chapters.body:
The Susquehanna Foundation and allied charitable vehicles support education and Philadelphia-area organizations. Yass-related funding has also reached free-market institutions abroad, including Israel's Kohelet Policy Forum [[inside-philanthropy-2026, haaretz-kohelet-2021]].

These channels are less transparent than FEC contributions. The profile separates documented grants from political spending and does not infer control from support alone [[inside-philanthropy-2026]].

chapters.title: Present influence
chapters.dek: A donor active in both policy and the 2026 cycle
chapters.body:
By late 2026, Yass remained an active funder of Club for Growth Action, MAGA Inc. and candidate-specific super PACs. Current-cycle totals are provisional until filings close [[forbes-yass-2026-giving, fec-yass]].

His influence rests on three reinforcing assets: SIG wealth, durable school-choice institutions and large checks to groups that shape Republican primaries. ByteDance adds a fourth channel—and an unusually direct financial stake in a live federal policy dispute [[wapo-school-choice-2025, axios-tiktok-2024]].
